payload.friendly_name: Concurrent writers to a Mission's files never lose or steal a write
payload.purpose_context: Parallel agents on one Mission routinely overlap: implement claims, move-task, add-history, tracer-append. Today several of these writers read-modify-write or roll back without the Mission's lock, so a command that exited 0 can have its committed write erased, or two claims can both pass a single-writer check. This Mission routes every Mission-file mutation through one locked primitive and keeps ad-hoc unlocked writes out with an architectural gate.
payload.purpose_tldr: Two agents writing the same Mission at once never silently lose, steal or corrupt each other's status, WP, tracer or claim writes.

payload.question: Which issues does this Mission fix, and which half of #5099 is in scope?

payload.final_answer: All of #5819, #5467, #5820, #5796, #5468, #5804 in full; #5099 only its one-writer-per-checkout half (atomic single_branch claim + advisory shared-workspace warning + doctrine sentence). The git add -A / git stash half stays with the upgrade-migration-commit-scope mission (#5443). Operator brief 2026-10-07.

payload.question: Which lock guards Mission-file mutation: a new mechanism or the existing per-mission status lock?

payload.final_answer: Reuse the existing per-mission feature_status_lock (keyed on the Mission directory name under the git common dir) as the one Mission write lock; add one checkout-wide claim lock only for the single_branch occupancy check, modelled on the verdict-save queue. No parallel per-file locks. Operator brief + #5819/#5804 triage (lock-held, tail-verified rollback as one fix).

payload.question: What may a failed status commit's rollback remove from status.events.jsonl?

payload.final_answer: Only rows it appended itself in the same lock hold, never a row already committed at HEAD, never when the log shrank or the tail does not parse; on refusal it leaves the log intact and says so loudly. Start from PR #4072's status/rollback.py design (operator ruling on #5819, 2026-10-07).

payload.question: Should a second writer in a shared checkout be refused or warned?

payload.final_answer: implement claims in a single_branch shared checkout stay REFUSED (existing WRITE_CHECKOUT_OCCUPIED, now atomic); review/implement in a workspace another actor holds in_progress/in_review get an advisory warning only (blocking refusal is #3129's product decision, per #5099 triage).
